metadata.note: The Binghamton Railway Company and its predecessors/successors: streetcar and interurban trolley service in Binghamton, Johnson City, Endicott and the surrounding Triple Cities area of Broome County, NY, roughly 1868-1932. Mass transit in the area began in 1868 with the horse-drawn Binghamton and Port Dickinson Railroad. The Washington Street and State Asylum Railroad (1871-1888) briefly operated the first electrified railroad in New York State (1887, Van Depoele system) before reverting to horse traction and ceasing operation; it is not drawn here (see the state-hospital feature's note). The system consolidated into the Binghamton Railway Company in 1901 (merging the Binghamton Railroad Company and the leased Binghamton, Lestershire and Union Railroad Company -- B,L&U's own name directly names the three places it served: Binghamton, Lestershire (renamed Johnson City in 1916), and Union, the township that became the village of Endicott). Foreclosed and reorganized as Triple Cities Traction Company in 1929, the system abandoned streetcar service line by line through 1932, starting with the Spring Forest car line (1927, before Triple Cities Traction even existed) and ending July 30, 1932 with the Ross Park and State Hospital/Leroy Street-Beethoven Street lines -- the first transit system in a major New York State metropolitan area to go all-bus.

metadata.geometry_sources: All geometry is street-centreline routing along present-day roads (not a traced track alignment), per the user's request to use modern-day roads for a street-running trolley network. See each feature's geometry_source/geometry_quality.
not_yet_sourced: Exact opening dates for the North Chenango, State Hospital, Leroy Street/Beethoven Street, Ross Park, Spring Forest and Johnson City-East Conklin lines are not documented in sources consulted; conservative placeholder dates (the 1868 B&PD charter for North Chenango, 1901 Binghamton Railway founding for the others) are used and flagged per-segment.
The corporate chain between the 1868 Binghamton and Port Dickinson Railroad Co. charter and the 1892-1901 'Binghamton Railroad' company named by one source is not established.

Whether streetcar service to the State Hospital continued unbroken between the 1888 end of the Washington Street and State Asylum Railroad and the 1901 Binghamton Railway Company is not documented -- treated here as an unsourced gap, not a claim of continuous service.

The exact location of 'East Conklin' (as named in the Johnson City-East Conklin car line) is not identified in any modern source or gazetteer; the drawn terminus near Conklin Center is an approximation.

The Endicott Shuttle car line (abandoned April 8, 1932 per CPTDB) is NOT included in this file -- no source found describes its route or termini distinctly from the West Endicott car line's Main Street corridor, so it was omitted rather than guessed.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates (see speed_source on each feature); no timetable was found for any line in this file.

properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING along Court Street, Main Street (Binghamton/West Side), Main Street through Johnson City, George F Highway and East Main Street into Endicott, then Madison Avenue/East Main Street/West Main Street to the west edge of Endicott's built-up area (~42.0918,-76.0904), the westernmost point where a named 'West Main Street' segment survives in OSM -- taken as a reasonable proxy for the historic West Endicott terminus. 502 points, ~15.3 km one-way (leg ratios 1.02-1.05 vs straight-line, i.e. essentially direct). segments.note: Reaches the Binghamton State Hospital (the former New York State Inebriate Asylum) via Chenango and Robinson Streets. An earlier and physically distinct predecessor, the Washington Street and State Asylum Railroad (1871-1888), served the same institution by a different, steeper route via Washington Street and a cable incline that had ceased operating by 1888; no source found documents exactly when or how streetcar service to the hospital resumed under this Robinson Street alignment, so 1901 (the Binghamton Railway Company's founding) is used as a conservative start with the 1888-1901 gap left unsourced.

properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING along Court Street, Chenango Street, then Robinson Street east to the Binghamton State Hospital grounds (the former New York State Inebriate Asylum, 425 Robinson Street). 173 points, ~4.5 km one-way, ratio 1.09. NOTE ON ERA: an earlier, physically distinct predecessor -- the Washington Street and State Asylum Railroad, incorporated 1871 -- reached the same institution via Washington Street and a 10% grade cable incline, and ceased operating in 1888 per Wikipedia. That alignment is NOT drawn here: Washington Street itself is a short (~1 km) downtown street nowhere near Robinson Street, and the cable incline's own right-of-way is not identifiable in the modern road network, so it cannot be honestly traced from present-day streets. This feature instead draws only the Robinson-Street-routed line documented as operating under Binghamton Railway Company; see metadata.

properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING: Main Street from Johnson City into downtown Binghamton, then Conklin Avenue and Conklin Road east/southeast along the Susquehanna's north bank into the Town of Conklin, ending near present-day Conklin Center (~42.036,-75.807), close to the town's geographic centroid. 640 points, ~19.5 km one-way. The Conklin Avenue/Road leg alone is ~13.9 km with ratio 1.29 against straight-line -- consistent with the road's real winding path along the river valley, not a routing artifact (the path was constrained to stay on named Conklin Avenue/Conklin Road the whole way, not found by unconstrained shortest-path search). 'East Conklin' does not appear as a distinct place in modern gazetteers or OSM place nodes -- the nearest documented hamlets are Conklin Center, Conklin Forks and Conklin Station, all further southeast along the same road. The terminus used here is therefore an approximation of an undocumented historic place name, not a confirmed endpoint.
